s1.syndrome_frame: excessive sweating of the buttocks and sacrum with significant impact on daily life

previous successful treatment of axillary hyperhidrosis with 20% aluminum chloride
unsuccessful treatment of intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride
key_facts: 31-year-old male nursing student
history of axillary hyperhidrosis
excessive sweating of the buttocks
most severe sweating at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum
previous treatment with 20% aluminum chloride for axillary hyperhidrosis
unsuccessful treatment with aluminum chloride for intergluteal cleft and sacrum
uses absorbent pads due to severity of condition
unable to attend work due to condition
Minor starch-iodine test performed to localize areas of overactive sweating
significant sweating identified in sacral region (10 × 3-cm area) and intergluteal cleft (6 × 8-cm area)

shortlist.label: Primary Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of axillary hyperhidrosis and now presents with excessive sweating of the buttocks, consistent with primary hyperhidrosis.

shortlist.label: Compensatory Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's previous treatment with aluminum chloride for axillary hyperhidrosis may have led to compensatory sweating in other areas, such as the buttocks.

shortlist.label: Localized Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's excessive sweating is localized to the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, consistent with localized hyperhidrosis.

shortlist.label: Generalized Hyperhidrosis

shortlist.label: Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of excessive sweating are consistent with hyperhidrosis, although this is a more general term.

shortlist.label: Gustatory Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, gustatory hyperhidrosis is a possible diagnosis if patient's sweating is triggered by food or drink.

shortlist.label: Secondary Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's excessive sweating could be secondary to an underlying medical condition, although none are mentioned in the case context.

shortlist.label: Frey Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Frey syndrome is a rare condition characterized by excessive sweating and flushing in response to food, which could be considered in this case.
